idiom_name: hand-written mapper class hierarchy (virtual load/save) mirroring the domain hierarchy
implementation_notes: The book's literal form works unchanged: an abstract mapper declares the protocol (virtual load/save plus the find/insert/update/delete members) and one concrete mapper per class overrides it, with dynamic dispatch through a base-class reference doing the work of 'a structure to organize database mappers'. For Class Table Inheritance the subclass mapper calls the superclass mapper for the inherited slice and then fills its own columns; for Single Table Inheritance the hierarchy collapses into one mapper plus a factory that switches on the discriminator column; for Concrete Table Inheritance the mappers are independent and simply duplicate the base column list. ODB is the library alternative that generates these mappers from '#pragma db object polymorphic' metadata.
pitfalls: Object slicing: a mapper that returns domain objects by value loses the subclass; the mapper protocol must hand back pointers or unique_ptr.
A virtual call in a constructor or destructor dispatches to the class currently under construction, so mapper registration or strategy setup must not live there.
Raw mapper pointers in a registry dangle when the registry is cleared while a session or Unit of Work still holds them; own mappers (unique_ptr/shared_ptr) and say who outlives whom.

variants.name: ODB polymorphic object hierarchy (#pragma db object polymorphic)
variants.implementation_notes: ODB generates the mapper code from metadata: marking the root class polymorphic and letting derived classes reuse the hierarchy makes the ODB compiler emit a table-per-hierarchy or table-per-class mapping chosen per class (table(...) pragmas), and loading a base-class object returns the derived instance. The mapper hierarchy therefore exists only in the generated code - the developer writes queries against base-class pointers and ODB resolves the discriminator. Choose it when the project already depends on ODB's compiler; otherwise the hand-written mappers are the smaller commitment.
pitfalls: The ODB compiler is a build step: generated mapper code and the pragma metadata must be regenerated whenever the hierarchy changes, or the mapping silently lags.
Virtual destructors are mandatory on polymorphic roots; without them deleting through a base pointer is undefined behaviour before it is a mapping bug.
Polymorphic pointers pull the whole hierarchy into the database schema: changing a base-class pragma can require migrating every subclass table.
variants.idiom_name: #pragma db object polymorphic on the hierarchy root
